COMMITTING: git push is 403 'denied to Onyx-Node' for the fixer too, not only for subagents - the App has no write access to kavopdf/app over HTTPS git. It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. The next run should commit that way, then 'git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main' so HEAD matches origin, then chain.py. chain.py's sync check is strict SHA equality and also refuses a dirty tree, and it rewrites CHAIN.json - so commit CHAIN.json again after each chain.py run.

context: 041122 and its fillable twin render 11 pages against the source's 9 (they were 12). The engine now CARRIES THE PAGE'S ADVANCE WIDTHS: DocxWriter writes a run in Arial with w:w = the scale that reproduces the width the page drew, whenever the PDF's face is not in READER_FACES (Arial/Helvetica/Liberation/DejaVu/Noto/Times/Courier/Calibri/Cambria/Georgia/Verdana/Tahoma/Symbol/Webdings, PDF subset tags stripped). Measured this run, all of it: the reader honours w:w (a correct scale gives the verification block 17 lines and 230 pt against 26 lines and 338 pt), and it IGNORES an embedded font part completely (built one, rendered it: 12 pages, NotoSans, geometry identical to baseline) and ignores w:fitText and w:noWrap. The carry-over's premise was wrong and is now measured wrong: the source's pitch in that cell is 12.00 pt exactly (baselines 579.61/591.61/603.61/615.61), the 240 tw w:line is that pitch, and the 4630 tw row is 16 lines at 240 tw plus 562 tw of paragraph gaps = 4642 tw written, 0.6 pt. What is left on 041122 is TWO spurious pages: our p8 (the page-7 folio, one line '7' at y=25.3) and our p10 (17 lines of the instruction page's spill). The folio rule added this run anchors a folio that reaches flowFromBox and it fixed source page 6, but page 7's folio is emitted as a TABLE CELL - a TableText paragraph inside the page's table - so the rule never sees it.
